Wolters Kluwer Health is seeking an Enterprise Software Engineer – Cloud Systems to build, automate, monitor, and improve cloud infrastructure and engineering platforms supporting its software products. The role contributes to reliable, scalable, secure, and performant development, testing, and production environments through cloud engineering, automation, observability, and site reliability practices.

Responsibilities
Assist with designing, implementing, and supporting cloud and on-premises infrastructure
Develop automation that improves the reliability and consistency of development, testing, and production environments
Contribute to cloud-native solutions using Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, or similar cloud platforms
Help create and maintain infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code and configuration-management practices
Support containerized applications and container-orchestration platforms
Contribute to continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines
Help improve monitoring, logging, alerting, and observability across applications and infrastructure
Use system metrics and key performance indicators to evaluate platform health, performance, and stability
Troubleshoot software, infrastructure, deployment, and performance issues using logs, metrics, alerts, and other technical evidence
Collaborate with software engineers, cloud engineers, quality teams, and other technical partners to resolve issues and improve system reliability
Compare possible technical solutions, identify advantages and trade-offs, and contribute to team decisions
Participate in code reviews, iterative planning, and agile development practices
Document technical solutions, operating procedures, and engineering best practices
Follow secure engineering practices for cloud access, authentication, authorization, and secrets management
Learn and apply new cloud technologies, programming languages, automation tools, and reliability-engineering practices

Required
Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related technical field
Academic, personal, or professional experience with software development, scripting, system administration, cloud computing, or infrastructure automation
Experience with at least one programming or scripting language, such as Python, Go, Groovy, PowerShell, Bash, or another shell-scripting language
Foundational understanding of operating systems, networks, software applications, or cloud infrastructure
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to investigate technical issues using logs, metrics, test results, and other available evidence
Interest in learning cloud technologies, automation tools, container platforms, and site reliability engineering practices
Ability to communicate clearly and collaborate effectively in a team environment
Commitment to system reliability, security, accountability, and continuous learning
Preferred
Exposure to Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, or another cloud platform
Familiarity with Linux, Unix, or Windows operating systems
Experience with Git or another source-control platform
Exposure to infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Azure Resource Manager, or AWS CloudFormation
Familiarity with Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, or another container and orchestration platform
Exposure to configuration-management tools such as Ansible
Familiarity with CI/CD technologies such as Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Actions
Exposure to monitoring or observability technologies such as Datadog, Splunk, the Elastic Stack, or OpenTelemetry
Familiarity with APIs, microservices, or enterprise API-management concepts
Understanding of cloud authentication, authorization, role-based access control, identity and access management, or secrets management
Exposure to agile practices or collaboration tools such as Scrum, Kanban, Jira, or Confluence
Interest in site reliability engineering, DevOps, platform engineering, cloud engineering, or release engineering
